title: ENV, EXPOSE, ARG & Labels 🏷️
description: Configure environment variables, declare ports, pass build arguments, and add metadata.

slides.title: `ENV` – Setting Environment Variables 🌍
slides.content:
# Persistent Variables for the Image

```dockerfile
ENV <key> <value>
# or
ENV <key>=<value>
```

Variables set with ENV are available:
- During the build (in subsequent RUN instructions)
- At runtime (inside the container)

**Example:**
```dockerfile
ENV NODE_ENV production
ENV APP_HOME /usr/src/app
WORKDIR $APP_HOME
```

You can override ENV variables at runtime with `-e`:
```bash
docker run -e NODE_ENV=development myimage
```

quizData.question: When does an ENV variable take effect?

options.text: Both during build and at runtime
Only if the container is started with `-e`

quizData.explanation: ENV sets an environment variable in the image that is available during subsequent build steps and inside running containers.

slides.title: `EXPOSE` – Documenting Ports 🚪
slides.content:
# Informational, Not Functional

```dockerfile
EXPOSE <port> [<port>/<protocol>...]
```

- `EXPOSE 80` tells Docker that the container listens on port 80.
- It does **not** publish the port to the host! That's done with `-p` at runtime.
- It serves as documentation and can be used by `-P` (publish all exposed ports to random host ports).

**Example:**
```dockerfile
EXPOSE 8080/tcp
```

> Think of it as a hint: “This container will need port 8080”.

quizData.question: `EXPOSE 3000` in a Dockerfile automatically makes the container accessible on localhost:3000 when you run it.
quizData.explanation: EXPOSE only documents the port; you still need `-p 3000:3000` (or `-P`) to actually map it.

slides.title: `ARG` – Build‑Time Variables 🔧
slides.content:
# Variables for `docker build`

```dockerfile
ARG <name>[=<default value>]
```

- ARG is available **only during build** (not at runtime).
- You can pass a value with `--build-arg`:
  ```bash
  docker build --build-arg VERSION=1.2 .
  ```

**Example:**
```dockerfile
ARG APP_VERSION=unknown
RUN echo "Building version $APP_VERSION"
```

> Use ARG for things like version numbers, download URLs, or temporary build secrets (but be careful: ARG values persist in image history).

quizData.question: When would you use ARG instead of ENV?

options.text: To set environment variables that the container needs at runtime
To pass build‑time values that are not needed after the image is built

quizData.explanation: ARG is for build‑only parameters, like selecting a package version during build. ENV is for runtime configuration.

slides.title: `LABEL` – Adding Metadata 🏷️
slides.content:
# Describe Your Image

```dockerfile
LABEL <key>=<value> <key2>=<value2>
```

Adds custom metadata to the image. Useful for version, maintainer, description.

**Example:**
```dockerfile
LABEL maintainer="john@example.com"
LABEL version="1.0"
LABEL description="This is my awesome app."
```

You can view labels with `docker inspect`.

slides.title: Full Example with ENV, EXPOSE, ARG, LABEL 🎨
slides.content: A Dockerfile for a Node.js app:
slides.codeSnippet:
FROM node:18-alpine
LABEL maintainer="me@example.com"
ARG NODE_ENV=production
ENV NODE_ENV=$NODE_ENV
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
